description: tidywater is an R package published by Brown and Caldwell contributors for joining water-chemistry and empirical treatment models. It represents a water-quality state and passes it through functions for chemical dosing and removal processes, so users can assemble a treatment train. Inputs include raw-water pH, alkalinity, dissolved constituents and chemical doses. Outputs are predicted water-quality variables after each modelled step for a single case or a data frame of scenarios. Geographic coverage is user-defined, and results apply to the supplied water, not a built-in utility. The README provides CRAN and GitHub installation, worked coagulation examples and links to vignettes. The LICENSE.md file grants a free choice between MIT and Apache-2.0 terms. That choice applies to the package code, while the source data and plant models require their own checks. A limitation is that its empirical functions require local calibration before plant-operating decisions. It can compare drinking-water treatment scenarios, whereas the catalogue's EPANET models distribution hydraulics. No plant measurements or R package were downloaded.
inputs: Raw-water quality and treatment chemical doses
name: tidywater drinking-water treatment models
